hints.content: The numerator of $~\dfrac{{{e}^{n}}}{n^2}~$ is an exponential function, and the denominator is a quadratic polynomial. The exponential function grows much faster than any polynomial function.  To see this, imagine letting $~n=100\,$.  The numerator would have $~100~$ factors of $~e\,$, which is a huge number!  At the same time, the denominator would have just $~2~$ factors of $~100\,$.

As $n\to \infty$, the numerator of the sequence grows much faster than the denominator.  

Hence,$\qquad\displaystyle\underset{n\to \infty }{\mathop{\lim }}\,\text{ }\frac{{{e}^{n}}}{n^2}=\infty\,$.
